Congenital splitting of the spinal cord within one dural sac; the associated bony spur does not establish a separate skeletal disorder.

Congenital postaxial extra digits; no evidence of additional organ disease.
Congenital bilateral enlargement of renal calyces.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of the stomach; no established common extra-gastric organ damage.
Macular retinal degeneration and local capillary abnormalities impair central vision; no systemic vascular or neurologic involvement established.

Benign or malignant tumor originating in a cutaneous hair follicle.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; developmental delay 3/3, proximal weakness/elevated CK 2/2, ptosis 3/3 and ophthalmoplegia 1/2; respiratory failure does not establish intrinsic lung damage.

Pre-existing antidonor antibodies cause complement-mediated vascular injury and thrombosis; the affected graft organ is unspecified.
Congenital ichthyosis with a resolving collodion membrane; restricted joint movement from tight skin does not establish lasting joint damage.
Anemia caused by protein deficiency; no additional intrinsic organ damage is specified.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising within a peripheral nerve, defining both neural location and blood-vessel origin.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the meninges; the definition overrides the erroneous salpingitis ancestry.
Oligodendroglial tumor located in the spinal cord.
Glycolytic defect defined by hemolysis and neurodegeneration; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%; immune dysfunction omitted at cap; respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
CDON-related forebrain cleavage malformation; frequencies of cleft palate and other extra-neural abnormalities are unspecified.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated FSH and depleted follicular reserve; hormonal dysfunction warrants the endocrine axis.
Ureteral disease belongs to the urinary axis; infectious and neoplastic mechanisms are not universal across this umbrella.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with vertebral, pelvic and epiphyseal abnormalities; microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction.
Disorder of skin keratinization causing scaling and desquamation; associated atopic diseases are separate conditions.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect; bruising and mucosal bleeding do not establish separate skin, airway or gastrointestinal organ disease.
